sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:64856
Court No. - 71
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 49484 of 2023

Applicant :- Pradeep Kumar @ Sher Singh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Upendra Upadhyay
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Akhilendra Yadav,G.A.
Hon'ble Mrs. Sadhna Rani (Thakur),J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the first informant and perused the record.

This application has been moved by the applicant Pradeep Kumar @ Sher Singh to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No. 85 of 2023 under Sections 498A, 323, 307, 504 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act Police Station Awagarh, District Etah.

entities.text: D.P. Act Police Station Awagarh, District Etah
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is argued by the learned counsel for the applicant that in the FIR the allegation is of demand of dowry.

In continuation of this demand, there was an altercation between the applicant and the injured 15 days prior to the incident and following that altercation only on 16.04.2023 at about 8.00 a.m. the applicant, his mother Munni Devi and sister Neelam poured petrol on the injured and set her ablaze.
In the statement of the injured, she has stated that the husband poured petrol on her and her sister-in-law caught hold her hands and the mother-in-law lit the fire.
It is further argued that the mother-in-law has been granted bail by the coordinate bench of this court.
In fact, the victim herself set her on fire because of the dispute with her husband.

It was her husband only, who took Pradeep Kumar @ Sher Singh vs State Of U.P. on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199512410/
1 her to the hospital, got her treated and Rs. 1,50,000/- was spent in her treatment, which were borne by the husband.

entities.text: Pradeep Kumar @ Sher Singh vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no criminal history to the credit of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 29.06.2023, hence, the prayer for bail is made.

Learned counsel for the first informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that from the FIR itself it is clear that previously also an FIR was lodged against the applicant, which was withdrawn after seeking excuse by the applicant and now in case of burning his wife alive the present applicant has been implicated, he is the most responsible person for the well being of his wife being husband of the victim.
From perusal of the record, it is found that in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. the victim has stated that her husband poured petrol on her, while her mother-in-law set her on fire.
She has suffered 55% to 60% burns.
The mother-in-law of the injured has been bailed out by the coordinate bench of this court.
Admittedly, the expenses of the treatment of the injured were borne by the husband himself.
There is no criminal history to the credit of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 29.06.2023.

Perusing the record, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the nature of allegations,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for granting bail to the applicant.
The bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant Pradeep Kumar @ Sher Singh involved in the aforesaid case be released on bail on furnishing personal bonds and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to the following conditions:-
1. The applicant will attend and co-operate the trial proceedings pending before the court concerned on the date fixed after release.
2. He will not tamper with the witnesses.
3. He will not indulge in any illegal activities during the bail period.

The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by the court concerned and in case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.

It is clarified that the observations, if any, made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of this bail application and must not be construed to have any reflection on the ultimate merits of the case.

Order Date :- 15.4.2024 gp  Pradeep Kumar @ Sher Singh vs State Of U.P. on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199512410/
